Detect unusual annual rates or quality indicators

Source: R/detect_anomaly.R
detect_anomaly.Rd

detect_anomaly() identifies annual observations that deserve review in outputs from create_asr() or create_quality(). The default "uncertainty" method compares consecutive years on the log-rate scale and uses the standard errors implied by the underlying counts or reported variances. The "robust" method compares each observation with the historical median using the median absolute deviation (MAD).

Usage

detect_anomaly(
  x,
  metrics = NULL,
  method = c("uncertainty", "robust"),
  by = NULL,
  year = "year",
  threshold = 3,
  min_history = 4,
  multiplier = 1e+05,
  zero_policy = c("exclude", "include"),
  variance_scale = c("display", "unmultiplied")
)

# S3 method for class 'asr'
detect_anomaly(
  x,
  metrics = NULL,
  method = c("uncertainty", "robust"),
  by = NULL,
  year = "year",
  threshold = 3,
  min_history = 4,
  multiplier = 1e+05,
  zero_policy = c("exclude", "include"),
  variance_scale = c("display", "unmultiplied")
)

# S3 method for class 'asrs'
detect_anomaly(
  x,
  metrics = NULL,
  method = c("uncertainty", "robust"),
  by = NULL,
  year = "year",
  threshold = 3,
  min_history = 4,
  multiplier = 1e+05,
  zero_policy = c("exclude", "include"),
  variance_scale = c("display", "unmultiplied")
)

# S3 method for class 'quality'
detect_anomaly(
  x,
  metrics = NULL,
  method = c("uncertainty", "robust"),
  by = NULL,
  year = "year",
  threshold = 3,
  min_history = 4,
  multiplier = 1e+05,
  zero_policy = c("exclude", "include"),
  variance_scale = c("display", "unmultiplied")
)

# S3 method for class 'qualities'
detect_anomaly(
  x,
  metrics = NULL,
  method = c("uncertainty", "robust"),
  by = NULL,
  year = "year",
  threshold = 3,
  min_history = 4,
  multiplier = 1e+05,
  zero_policy = c("exclude", "include"),
  variance_scale = c("display", "unmultiplied")
)

# Default S3 method
detect_anomaly(
  x,
  metrics = NULL,
  method = c("uncertainty", "robust"),
  by = NULL,
  year = "year",
  threshold = 3,
  min_history = 4,
  multiplier = 1e+05,
  zero_policy = c("exclude", "include"),
  variance_scale = c("display", "unmultiplied")
)

Arguments

x

An object returned by create_asr() or create_quality(). Objects returned with collapse = FALSE are also supported.

metrics

Character vector of metric columns to check. For asr objects the default is c("cr", "asr_wld85"); for quality objects the default is c("inci", "mort", "mv", "mi").

method

Detection method: "uncertainty" compares consecutive years, while "robust" uses the historical median and MAD.

by

Character vector of columns defining independent time series. The default uses the available columns among regicode, sex, and cancer.

year

Name of the year column. Defaults to "year".

threshold

Absolute score at which an observation is flagged. Defaults to 3.

min_history

Minimum number of usable historical values required by the robust method. Defaults to 4.

multiplier

Rate multiplier used by create_asr() and create_quality(). For ASR variance columns, it is used only when variance_scale = "unmultiplied". Defaults to 100000.

zero_policy

Whether zero-valued observations are excluded from comparisons or included where the selected method permits it. The default is "exclude".

variance_scale

Scale of ASR variance columns. The default, "display", matches current create_asr() output. Use "unmultiplied" for legacy variance columns. Standard-error columns are always interpreted on the displayed rate scale.

Value

A tibble with one row per input observation and metric. It includes grouping columns, year, metric, value, expected, se, reference_se, scale, score, p_value, direction, anomaly, and status.

Details

This function is intended for quality-control screening. An anomaly flag is not evidence that a registry value is wrong, and the unadjusted p_value returned by the uncertainty method is not a substitute for a prespecified trend model or multiplicity-adjusted inference.

References

International Agency for Research on Cancer. Cancer Incidence in Five Continents, Volume XII: Statistical methods for registries. https://publications.iarc.who.int/_publications/media/download/3523/

See also

create_asr(), create_quality()

Examples

data("canregs")
fbsws <- count_canreg(canregs)
asr <- create_asr(
  fbsws,
  year,
  show_var = TRUE,
  collapse = TRUE
)
detect_anomaly(asr, metrics = "asr_wld85")
